submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole fires when the clause under way predicates something about a person: activation climbs through the first few tokens of the predicate (the copula or auxiliary - is, was, are, am, have, can - a predicate adverb such as 'also', 'not', 'mainly', or a possessive/relative pronoun that refers back to the person: his, who, or its for an organisation) whenever the clause's subject denotes a human being (a name, he/she/I/you, a human noun phrase) or a body of people (an organisation, committee, institution, family). It falls to near zero when the identical predicate is applied to an inanimate or abstract subject ('the building', 'the machine', 'the protein', 'it') - the same surface token ('also', 'very', 'was') is typically 2-4x weaker, so the personhood of the subject, not the token identity, sets the strength.
